transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes (scheduled 15:00-15:52)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood CSM), Liam O'Neill (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Auriga Head of Platform), Evan Brooks (Auriga SRE), Monique Lee (Auriga Security), Samir Patel (Auriga Dev Lead)

Summary (auto):
Quick simulation of the recovery plan after the KV-cache fragmentation incident last week; confirm priority patch and canary rollout; align on smoke test window and data/sample handoff; address security audit concerns about logs and KMS access during rollback.

Topics: recovery simulation, KV cache replay, canary rollout, telemetry gaps, security/KMS access, SLA implications, next steps and owners.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: okay hi everyone thanks for jumping on happy monday, i know this is short notice, we'll run through the rapid recovery sim and handoff the priority patch, um Diego will take the technical bits.
[00:17] Priya Nair: thanks Maya, appreciate it. quick note, Evan's got the recent traces ready but delayed on redaction, i'll send later in the call.
[00:25] Diego Ramos: hey all, yeah i'll start with a quick tl;dr of root cause as we understand it — KV cache fragmentation plus a rare race on eviction under burst writes, compounded by prefix caching mismatch between two autoscale pods, which caused stale token references.
[00:45] Evan Brooks: uh that matches our observation, we saw a spike in tail latency and then a series of 5xx that correlated with a cache invalidation that didn't propagate.
[00:56] Samir Patel: one thing — i think one of the pods was running an older quantized variant? there was a mismatch in model surface, maybe that confused the runtime.
[01:08] Liam O'Neill: yeah that's important — Diego, was there evidence that model variant mismatch fast-failed the KV mapping?
[01:15] Diego Ramos: partial, we have logs that suggest the kernel selector chose a different execution path and that changed the KV key format, so during a rapid promote the lookup failed. also, small note — some names in the logs were transcribed odd, like 'K-V cash' in our early notes, so apologies.
[01:34] Monique Lee: security angle — during the incident we saw multiple KMS errors in the audit log when we tried to rotate keys as part of our mitigation, is that expected?
[01:42] Diego Ramos: no, that's not expected. we think the rotation attempt collided with the rollback window; the KMS calls hit a rate limit because the remediation automation retried aggressively. i'm going to add rate-limit backoff in the script.
[01:57] Priya Nair: ok good — we need that to be explicit, Monique will still want a write-up for her audit.
[02:05] Monique Lee: yep and please include the exact KMS API call ids if possible — our compliance team will ask.
[02:12] Diego Ramos: noted. i'll surface the call ids in the runbook export.
[02:18] Maya Chen: short play: Diego runs through a dry run of the KV replay locally, then we schedule a small canary in prod in the smoke window, customer provides traces, we run the smoke test, then green rollout. does that reflect?
[02:33] Priya Nair: yes that matches. what about the fallback — if the canary fails what's the immediate rollback path?
[02:40] Diego Ramos: immediate rollback is to route traffic to a read-only variant and hot-swap the routing table, also flush KV prefix and rehydrate from the persisted snapshot. we'll detail steps.
[02:54] Evan Brooks: question — flushing the prefix is destructive for some sessions, any chance we can do a non-destructive rehydrate first?
[03:02] Diego Ramos: we can attempt non-destructive first for a small subset, but if the cache is corrupt it won't fix the mapping. i'll add an intermediate step: snapshot -> rehydrate to a test bucket, then swap.
[03:14] Samir Patel: is there a risk with continuous batching being in-flight and losing tokens during swap? we've had request-level state in-flight a few times.
[03:22] Diego Ramos: yes, continuous batching means in-flight KV will be stale; mitigation is drain connections on canary pods and use short TTL on prefix keys during switchover.
[03:31] Liam O'Neill: from the SLA and billing side, Priya, we wanted to confirm you won't need a credit for this window — or will you be asking for a contractual remedy?
[03:41] Priya Nair: we're evaluating impact on customer-facing latency, if the smoke test shows residual errors we will reopen the contract conversation. for now we want the mitigation to be rock-solid.
[03:52] Monique Lee: also, we need assurance about log redaction and PII during the runbook handoff — please keep traces anonymized.
[03:59] Diego Ramos: yes, we'll only ask for the minimum required traces and give redaction guidance.
[04:06] Maya Chen: Diego can you walk us through the simulated run now? even if it's high level.
[04:11] Diego Ramos: sure. step one: local replay — take sample trace, run the replay tool to exercise prefix eviction path, verify TTLs and key formats. step two: produce a small patch that normalizes key format at promote time — that prevents mismatched key formats. step three: dry-run on staging with same workload. step four: canary in prod with traffic steer of 3% for 15 minutes, collect success/error metrics. step five: if green, roll to 25% for 30 minutes then full roll. each step has explicit undo.
[04:45] Evan Brooks: for the canary metrics what thresholds are we using? latencies, error rates?
[04:50] Diego Ramos: threshold: tail p95 latency not increase by more than 15% vs baseline, 5xx rate < 0.1% of requests, cache miss delta within 2% of baseline.
[05:03] Priya Nair: baseline needs to be the last 24 hours pre-incident, can we compare?
[05:07] Diego Ramos: yes that's the plan. we'll pull the 24-hour baseline and include it in the canary dashboard.
[05:13] [00:05:14] Samir Patel: small side — any chance this is related to the earlier model swap we did two weeks ago? i still think the model pq file naming had changed.
[05:23] Diego Ramos: possible. Diego pauses, um — our onboarding pipeline should have normalized it but it did not. i'll add a normalization step in the promotion flow.
[05:34] [00:06:00] Monique Lee: security follow up — will the remediation involve granting Redwood engineers temporary KMS access? we have strict policies and need an auditable path.
[06:07] Liam O'Neill: we can use our support key-proxy flow so we never get direct KMS credentials; it's temporary, logged, and you remain the principle. we also have SSO/SAML logs for the session.
[06:19] Monique Lee: ok hard requirement: all actions must be audit-logged and we need the session ids.
[06:25] Diego Ramos: we'll include session ids and the runbook will include the exact commands to run the proxy flow, and the expiration TTL.
[06:33] Priya Nair: timeline expectations — can this be ready by end of week? our Q4 launch depends on it.
[06:40] Diego Ramos: we'll aim for the patch and canary plan by 2026-10-07 end of day. smoke test target 2026-10-08 morning as proposed.
[06:49] Maya Chen: great. now quick demo of the replay tool output (Diego shares screen) — sorry screen bail, but you can see the key mismatch error highlighted: keyFormatA != keyFormatB.
[07:02] Diego Ramos: right — here's the sample trace id 0x7a2f that shows eviction at t=137s and subsequent lookup failure.
[07:12] Evan Brooks: i recognized that trace — we'll attach the anonymized version after the call.
[07:16] [00:07:30] Samir Patel: can the patch be delivered as a hotfix (small binary) or is it a configuration change? we need to know rollback cost.
[07:26] Diego Ramos: it's a small change in the promotion code path — hotfix binary deployable as a psudo-patch, no model retrain. rollback is a simple routing swap.
[07:36] Monique Lee: do you need any additional auth to run the hotfix in our environment?
[07:41] Liam O'Neill: just the same support proxy flow and a runbook-signed approval from Priya.
[07:47] Priya Nair: i'll provide approval once i see the runbook and the smoke test plan.
[07:51] Diego Ramos: i'll include step-by-step checks for Monique's team to verify KMS audit entries.
[07:58] [00:09:00] Maya Chen: ok let's talk telemetry gaps — Evan you mentioned a missing marker that made it hard to trace the propagation window?
[09:09] Evan Brooks: yeah we lacked a consistent correlation id between the autoscale control plane and the runtime; logs had different request ids, so stitching was manual.
[09:18] Diego Ramos: we can add a short-term header passthrough that propagates a trace-id through the runtime chain; long-term we'll do universal correlation.
[09:27] Samir Patel: the side effect is we need to ensure header size doesn't blow up the batching metadata.
[09:33] Diego Ramos: agreed, we'll use a compact trace id and compress where possible.
[09:38] Priya Nair: for compliance Monique wants the log retention and masking clarified if we enable trace passthrough.
[09:45] Monique Lee: yes no PII in header, only generated ids.
[09:49] Diego Ramos: we'll publish the spec for generated ids, no user data.
[09:54] [00:10:15] Liam O'Neill: moving to SLA impact — if the canary fails and we do rollback there will be a short window of degraded throughput, what's Redwood's procedural SLA?
[10:24] Maya Chen: procedural SLA — we commit to communication, targeted mitigation windows, and a documented rollback plan; for credits we'll evaluate depending on exact impact but we'll treat this as priority one for resolution.
[10:36] Priya Nair: we want that in writing, Liam, can you update the contract note?
[10:41] Liam O'Neill: yes i'll update and send an addendum for the provisional remedial clause.
[10:46] [00:11:00] Diego Ramos: quick tech note — the KV cache replay tool currently supports staged replays with an "impact factor" you can dial; we'll run at 0.1 then 1.0. the script will also produce a dry-run report.
[11:14] Evan Brooks: nice, please include the dry-run log format so we can ingest it into our slack ops channel.
[11:20] Diego Ramos: will do.
[11:23] [00:12:00] Monique Lee: a quick question on retention — will the replay produce any persistent artifacts in Redwood's logs that we should be aware of?
[12:10] Diego Ramos: only ephemeral dry-run logs; persistent artifacts will be pushed to your s3 bucket or the staging project that you control. we won't retain your traces longer than needed.
[12:22] Monique Lee: perfect, please state that in the runbook.
[12:27] Priya Nair: if possible can we see a sample runbook skeleton now, even bullets?
[12:33] Diego Ramos: bullets: prerequisites (auth, redwood proxy steps), data requirements (trace ids and anonymization guidance), replay steps (local -> staging -> canary), validation checks (metrics and thresholds), rollback steps, postmortem notes and artifact collection.
[12:51] [00:13:00] Samir Patel: ok, any risk of the replay triggering the same fragmentation in staging? we don't want to corrupt staging caches.
[13:07] Diego Ramos: we'll use isolated namespaces and short TTLs; plus we run with reduced concurrency by default.
[13:14] [00:14:00] Priya Nair: timeline recap? Diego patch + runbook by 2026-10-07, traces by 2026-10-06, smoke test 2026-10-08 am — anyone object?
[14:06] Evan Brooks: no objections.
[14:10] Maya Chen: great. now a quick informal rolecall on ownership for audit artifacts — Monique you want the KMS call ids, Priya you want the redaction proof, Diego will produce the runbook.
[14:25] Monique Lee: correct.
[14:28] Diego Ramos: i'll annotate runbook with exact KMS call ids when possible and include the session proxy log sample.
[14:36] [00:15:00] Liam O'Neill: a couple of commercial notes — given the impact window we're offering a complimentary priority support week to help with the smoke test and followups, and a dedicated escalation channel.
[15:01] Priya Nair: appreciated, we'll take you up on that.
[15:05] [00:16:00] Samir Patel: small operational ask — can we get an ops playbook snippet showing how to detect KV fragmentation early? we'd like to add it to our runbook.
[16:18] Diego Ramos: yes, include metrics: rising eviction rate, sudden increase in miss ratio, and mismatch in key format hashes; we'll give some dashboards and alerts.
[16:29] Evan Brooks: also add a synthetic probe to failover to read-only variant to validate remap works.
[16:36] Diego Ramos: good idea.
[16:39] [00:17:00] Monique Lee: last security thing — for the audit we need a timeline of actions taken during the incident, can Redwood produce a short chronology?
[17:06] Maya Chen: yes we'll put together a chronology doc, Diego will draft the timeline and i will QA it for customer-facing wording.
[17:15] [00:18:00] Priya Nair: perfect. any blockers we haven't covered?
[18:02] Samir Patel: none on our side.
[18:04] Diego Ramos: none from engineering beyond the runbook and patch completion.
[18:09] [00:19:00] Maya Chen: ok let's confirm next steps — Diego, patch + runbook by 10/07, Priya send traces by 10/06, Maya schedule smoke test 10/08 09:00-09:30 PT, Liam update contract note by 10/09.
[19:28] Priya Nair: will do.
[19:31] Monique Lee: thanks everyone.
[19:33] [00:20:00] Diego Ramos: i'll also include a small checklist for Monique to validate KMS audit ids.
[20:41] Liam O'Neill: one last commercial clarification — if we needed additional dedicated capacity during the smoke test is Redwood able to temporarily allocate reserved slots?
[20:53] Diego Ramos: yes we can spin ephemeral dedicated capacity for the test if you want, it'll be in the canary plan and we can bill separately or include as a courtesy, we'll confirm.
[21:07] Priya Nair: include it as optional in the plan.
[21:11] [00:22:00] Maya Chen: any loose ends?
[22:03] Evan Brooks: just the redaction timing for traces, i need to coordinate with legal — i'll aim to get them to Priya by tomorrow.
[22:12] Priya Nair: thanks Evan.
[22:15] [00:23:00] Maya Chen: ok i'm going to read back the recap — patch + runbook (Diego) by 2026-10-07 EOD; traces (Customer) by 2026-10-06; smoke test 2026-10-08 09:00-09:30 PT; contract addendum (Liam) by 2026-10-09; follow-up call after smoke test (Maya) scheduled. please confirm in chat.
[23:02] Priya Nair: confirmed.
[23:05] Monique Lee: confirmed.
[23:07] Samir Patel: confirmed.
[23:09] Diego Ramos: confirmed.
[23:11] Liam O'Neill: confirmed.
[23:12] [00:24:00] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll send notes + runbook skeleton shortly, end call.
